projects.title: JPMorgan Chase: Legal Technology Strategy & Transformation
projects.tagline: Connected business priorities to technology strategy, product governance, multi-year roadmaps, financial and workforce planning, and executive decision-making across a global Legal Technology organization.
projects.description:
## The challenge

In Legal Technology, the challenge is not simply delivering isolated projects. It is aligning different product areas, technical teams, business partners, resources, and control obligations around a coherent set of priorities. I led the management processes that helped translate those priorities into plans, ownership, governance, and delivery accountability.

## My contribution

Annual strategy cycle, portfolio and roadmap alignment, financial and workforce planning, organizational operating-model improvements, executive reviews, and AI opportunity prioritization.

## Outcome

Helped establish clearer priorities, accountability, and decision-making across the technology portfolio.

projects.title: AI Engineering Factory & Analytics
projects.tagline: Built a supervised AI-assisted engineering system that coordinates planning, development, testing, independent review, and human release decisions, alongside a dashboard for delivery evidence and failure analysis.
projects.description:
## The problem

As a solo founder building multiple products, I needed more structured development capacity without losing control over code quality, security, ownership, or the release process.

## The system

I designed a governed workflow in which work is planned, assigned to specialized AI agents, isolated for implementation, checked through automated tests, reviewed independently, and presented for a human decision before release.

## The controls

Scoped task ownership, isolated work environments, security restrictions, testing and review requirements, bounded repair attempts, stop conditions, and recorded execution evidence.

## The analytics

A companion dashboard examines tasks, review outcomes, failures, timing, cost-related records where available, and evidence quality to make engineering performance more visible.

## What this demonstrates

Operating-system design for AI-assisted engineering; agent orchestration; quality governance; engineering metrics; traceability; and iterative improvement.

caseStudy.riskAndControls: Scoped task ownership, isolated work environments, security restrictions, testing and review requirements, bounded repair attempts, stop conditions, and recorded execution evidence.
caseStudy.howItWorks:
Every change moves through five phases.

**Govern and intake.** Requests from me, Jira or GitHub issues are reconciled into a ranked queue and revalidated before use. A task is picked only if it is unblocked, unclaimed and within the run budget, with up to three running in parallel.

**Triage and plan.** Work that is ready to build has an approved plan, clear acceptance criteria and bounded scope. Unclear or higher-risk work goes to planner agents, and a person reviews the plan. Missing information or conflicting requests are held for a person, never guessed.

**Build and validate.** One owner claims each task in its own isolated worktree. Specialist agents join only when needed. The implementer works inside the authorized scope and adds regression tests, then the project's quality gates run. Tests are never weakened to get a pass.

**Review and assure.** Independent reviewers run in parallel, chosen by what changed: code, security, AI behavior, UI and accessibility. Blocking findings get at most two repair cycles; then the system stops and asks.

**Approve and learn.** A passing change comes to me for approval before it merges into the protected main branch. Every run is recorded (hashes, not content) and feeds Factory Analytics (lead time, repair rate, review catch rate), which I use to tune the rules and agents.

Governance runs throughout: rules are enforced by hooks, high-risk work needs a person, secrets are scanned, and no agent approves its own work.

projects.title: Prepera
projects.tagline: Brings résumé optimization, job tracking, AI voice interview practice, and salary-negotiation preparation into one career workflow.
projects.description:
## The problem

A job search runs across a dozen tools: job boards, tracking spreadsheets, resume editors, interview-prep videos, salary forums. Prepera puts the whole search in one place and adds an AI coach at every step.

## What it does

Candidates search listings aggregated from major job boards, then track every application on a drag-and-drop pipeline that runs from Saved through Applied, Screening, Interview, and Offer. Email sync captures recruiter replies automatically. The AI layer tailors resumes to each role, runs practice interviews, and preps salary negotiation before the offer call.

## Status

In production at preperahq.com with Stripe billing.

## How it's built

Next.js and TypeScript on the front end, Supabase and Postgres behind it, with Claude and OpenAI powering the coaching features.

projects.title: AuthMatch AI
projects.tagline: Prior-authorization copilot that matches each case to Medicare coverage policy and shows reviewers which criteria are met.
projects.description:
## The problem

Insurance prior authorizations are slow because reviewers have to find the controlling Medicare policy for every case by hand. New CMS rules (CMS-0057-F, effective January 2026) put hard deadlines on that work: seven days for standard requests, 72 hours for expedited ones.

## What it does

AuthMatch matches each case, by HCPCS/CPT code and member state, to the controlling NCD or LCD policy and reads the clinical documentation against it. The reviewer sees each criterion marked Met, Not Met, or Indeterminate with the supporting evidence cited. A licensed human reviewer signs off on every case.

## Architecture

The Next.js reviewer UI is a thin shell that never touches PHI. All PHI processing, OCR, guideline matching, and LLM calls live in a FastAPI service. Postgres enforces row-level security, and an audit trigger logs every access. The design goal was strict PHI isolation and a defensible audit trail.

projects.title: Gen4Me
projects.tagline: Turns a one-line project idea into the CLAUDE.md, PRD, and build plan your AI coding agents need.
projects.description:
## The problem

AI coding agents are only as good as the context you give them, and most projects have stale docs or none at all.

## What it does

From a one-line description of your project, Gen4Me researches your stack on the live web, asks you to confirm its assumptions instead of guessing, and generates a tailored CLAUDE.md, a research-backed PRD, a build plan, and per-directory rules. As the codebase evolves, it audits the docs against the code and flags drift.

## How it's built

Next.js, TypeScript, Supabase, and Postgres, with LLM pipelines grounded by live web research.

projects.title: SanctionsWatch
projects.tagline: Monitors sanctions changes across U.S., U.K., E.U., U.N., and Canadian authorities and turns them into clear alerts for compliance teams.
projects.description:
## The problem

Sanctions lists change constantly across U.S., U.K., E.U., U.N., and Canadian authorities, and most compliance teams find out by reading raw regulatory text after the fact.

## What it does

SanctionsWatch ingests updates from each authority, deduplicates and classifies them, summarizes the impact with an LLM, and alerts the teams that need to act. The goal is an audit-ready trail from regulatory change to acknowledgment.

## How it's built

Next.js and TypeScript on Supabase and Postgres, with an ingestion pipeline built on Apify and n8n.

projects.title: G2 Complaint Miner
projects.tagline: CLI that mines G2 reviews for recurring complaints and scores them as AI product opportunities.
projects.description:
## The idea

Customer complaints are a product roadmap nobody reads, and G2 reviews are full of them.

## What it does

The CLI scrapes G2 reviews for target products, uses Claude to classify unstructured review text into complaint themes, and scores recurring pain points as candidate AI product opportunities. It's the research tool I use to decide what to build next.

## How it's built

TypeScript, Node.js, the Claude API, and Postgres.

about.name: Erick Clark
about.title: Technology Strategy & AI Transformation Professional
about.heroTagline: Former JPMorgan Chase Vice President and Chief of Staff with more than 15 years of experience across technology strategy, enterprise transformation, portfolio governance, and business operations. I also design and build AI-powered products, giving me direct experience connecting executive decisions to technical execution.
about.quote: I’ve never been satisfied with just understanding how something works. I want to know how to make it better.
bio: I'm a technology strategy and transformation executive with more than 15 years of experience across financial services, energy, technology services, and the U.S. Army.

Most recently, I served as Vice President and Chief of Staff for Legal Technology at JPMorgan Chase. My responsibilities connected technology strategy, product portfolio governance, financial and workforce planning, executive operations, and cross-functional execution. I worked with senior leaders and technology teams to translate priorities into plans, establish accountability, and move complex initiatives forward.

My experience extends beyond corporate strategy. I have led technology programs, supported large-scale modernization efforts, improved business processes, and managed initiatives across highly regulated environments.

In recent years, I've expanded into hands-on AI product development. I design and build applications involving language models, AI agents, data integrations, document intelligence, workflow automation, and cloud infrastructure. This has strengthened my understanding of the implementation challenges, technical decisions, and governance considerations that determine whether an AI initiative succeeds.
I also founded Clark Strategic Systems LLC, known publicly as Clark Strategics, to help organizations address technology challenges through consulting and implementation.

My perspective is shaped by both executive leadership and direct experience developing software. I understand the decisions required to fund and govern technology, along with the work involved in making it operational.

Credentials: Master of Business Administration (MBA); Master of Science, Management Information Systems; Bachelor of Science, Business & Accounting; Project Management Professional (PMP); Professional Scrum Master I (PSM I); AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner; FinOps Certified Practitioner; United States Army Veteran.
Identify the real problem. Make clear decisions. Deliver something that creates value.
